blocking_findings.title: R08 promises a three-sidecar rollback property that the current installer and proposed diffs cannot provide
evidence: install_book_sidecar_rows_v2.py atomically replaces each file separately in sequence, so the three-file set is not one atomic transaction.
If replacement or read-back fails on the second or third sidecar, earlier files remain replaced.
The installer holds no preimage backups or durable transaction journal, accepts no R07 snapshot or R05/R06 receipt, and removes the lock in finally even after partial failure.
The proposal says every failed replace retains all preinstall files, but proposes no installer revision and no failure-injection or recovery test.
required_remedy: Add a versioned installer implementation or adapter-scoped transactional wrapper; do not change v2 evidence in place.
Under the exclusive lock, require exact R07 snapshot SHA, latest passing R05/R06 receipt SHAs, render-manifest SHA, payload SHA, and current full/non-book sidecar hashes.
Build and fsync all three postimages before the first replace, persist exact preimages or recoverable backups plus a fsynced transaction journal, and record intended before/after hashes.

After each replace, read back and verify. On any failure, atomically restore every replaced preimage and verify all three full hashes. If restoration is incomplete, retain the lock and journal, emit recovery_required, and block all continuation.
Delete the lock only after a fully verified commit or fully verified rollback. Never call the three-file set atomic merely because each individual os.replace is atomic.
Add injected failures before replace, after replace one, after replace two, during read-back, and during rollback, plus stale-lock/journal recovery tests.
Add a runtime/filesystem capability probe or a scoped environment-bound exception for same-volume replace, fsync, and lock semantics.

blocking_findings.title: Post-render hash closure omits rendered artifacts and append-only receipts do not preserve failed render bytes
evidence: R04 declares decision evidence, book-local role artifacts, appeals/dissents, chunks, packets, relations, sidecar payload, and an invalid receipt as outputs.

R05 and R07 bind chunks, packets, relations, and sidecar payload but omit decision_evidence_v2.jsonl, appeal_ledger.jsonl, materialized primary/peer/boss role artifacts, and the pending post-resolution artifact.
The proposed adapter gives attempt-scoped paths to receipts but not to the rendered evidence itself, so a later repair can overwrite the bytes that a preserved failed receipt hashes.
A declarative invalidation matrix cannot detect drift in an artifact that no downstream receipt or manifest enumerates.
required_remedy: Define a typed R04 render manifest containing the exact closed output set, path, byte SHA-256, canonical row projection SHA-256 where applicable, row count, schema, and writer revision.
Store failed and passing render outputs under immutable run/attempt paths; publish a current-book projection only after R05 and required R06 pass.
Bind the complete render-manifest SHA and revalidated current bytes in R05, R06, R07, R08, R09, R10, and the completion receipt.
Add negative tests that mutate each rendered artifact class independently after R05 and after R07, including decision evidence, one role artifact, the appeal ledger, and sidecar payload.

blocking_findings.title: R00-R10 ordering is declarative rather than causally hash-chained
evidence: The lifecycle plan says R07 was created after R05/R06 and that completion is last, but it does not define a stage-receipt schema with predecessor hashes or controller-observed causal events.
The proposed exploit tests can reject obvious date order but do not prevent self-attested timestamps, mutable selection indexes, omitted failed attempts, or receipt substitution.
The existing T521 lesson already warns that timestamps alone cannot prove stage ordering.
required_remedy: Give every R00-R10 attempt an immutable receipt with run_id, stage ordinal, attempt_id, exact predecessor receipt SHA-256 values, controller assignment/result event IDs, input manifest SHA, output/render manifest SHA, status, and supersession rule.
Make the lifecycle validator derive causality from the hash DAG and immutable attempt inventory, never mtime or self-attested timestamps.
Add exploit tests for forged timestamps, a changed selected-attempt index, a hidden failed attempt, wrong predecessor SHA, stage skip, and replay of an old passing receipt.

blocking_findings.title: The proposed global identifier validator is not yet provider-neutral and is tested only with Hosea token shapes
evidence: VAL-R2-002 requires discovery of source-primary identifiers but does not define a typed, book-independent identifier inventory or source-artifact export contract.
All named exploit fixtures use HOS_Q and HOS_MACRO tokens.
The proposal's own residual risk admits that the provider-neutral inventory mechanism and non-Hosea exploit evidence are missing.
A global validator implemented from these examples could either hard-code Hosea prefixes or miss unrelated Hebrew, Aramaic, Greek, poetry, Gospel, epistle, and apocalyptic identifier shapes.
required_remedy: Define a typed source_identifier_inventory and active_identifier_registry schema, populated from frozen source artifacts rather than regex guesses or book prefixes.
Require provenance-only rows to bind inventory ID, source artifact path and SHA, identifier kind, operational=false, and an active replacement that resolves by kind, ID, and span.
Add synthetic provider-neutral fixtures with at least two unrelated namespaces and shapes, including a non-Hosea book, plus false-positive prose containing ordinary uppercase tokens.
Keep r2 at unverified_without_deterministic_r2_harness until those generic tests pass.

blocking_findings.title: The Hosea materializer cannot execute the proposed approved repair without an unplanned change
evidence: corrective_re_review_v2.py deliberately raises when newly rendered sidecar_rows_v2.json differs from the existing payload.

The accepted semantic repair changes defensible_basis for every unit, and sidecar_replacement writes defensible_basis into possible_downstream_risk for low or medium-low rows, so the new payload is expected to differ.
The proposal requires a new materialized Hosea attempt but supplies no exact environment-bound materializer delta or attempt-scoped output migration.
required_remedy: Add an exact, separately checked environment-bound materializer amendment that accepts only a hash-bound approved repair application receipt and writes a new attempt-scoped sidecar payload.
Do not delete the old payload or weaken the mismatch guard into an unconditional overwrite.
Prove the new payload hash from the amended route before materialization, preserve the old payload as failed-attempt evidence, and keep global sidecars untouched.

blocking_findings.title: The environment-bound exception lacks the ownership, expiry, and human-review fields required by portable capability governance
evidence: The proposal classifies the book materializer as environment_bound_exception.
The proposed adapter records runtime, path, classification, and event-based expiration triggers but no owner, fixed expiry or review deadline, human-review status, or exception approval receipt.
Candidate evidence may remain unactivated, but it cannot be treated as an approved environment-bound exception without those fields.
required_remedy: Either classify the current materializer as unapproved_environment_bound_candidate_evidence, or add owner, scope, human_review_status=pending, approval receipt requirement, expires_at or bounded review deadline, migration/rollback plan, and fail-closed activation rule.
Do not activate or claim an exception until the owner-reviewed receipt exists.
